messages:
Linh: Hey — hitting a weird auth loop with redwoodctl when using a custom profile for local dev. Installed via brew (redwoodctl 0.8.2). I run `redwoodctl auth login --profile team-local`, browser flow completes, CLI says login successful, but `redwoodctl whoami --profile team-local` returns "not authenticated". Anyone seen this?

Matt: hmm, first thought: where is your config/credentials being written? XDG_CONFIG_HOME vs ~/.config mismatch often bites.

Linh: I checked. ~/.config/redwood/config.yaml lists the profile but the token field is empty. The CLI output during login looked normal though: 
```
$ redwoodctl auth login --profile team-local
Opening https://auth.redwood.dev/...
Login successful
Stored credentials to /Users/linh/.config/redwood/credentials
```
But the file ends up empty.

Sam: are you on macOS or using WSL? Also did you ever run the CLI with sudo? If credentials file is root-owned that explains write failures.

Linh: macOS (M1). I did run one test command with sudo during an earlier install. I tried `redwoodctl auth login --profile team-local --debug` and saw `write /Users/linh/.config/redwood/credentials: permission denied`. `ls -la ~/.config/redwood` shows the credentials file owned by root.

Devex Bot: Known issue: installer sometimes creates config dir with root perms if `sudo` used during postinstall. See GH #1234 (internal). Workaround: chown the dir, avoid sudo for normal use. :robot_face:

Matt: quick safe fix (no sudo): `sudo chown $(whoami) ~/.config/redwood -R` then re-run `redwoodctl auth login --profile team-local`. Also double-check $XDG_CONFIG_HOME if set in shell. We'll triage to ensure installer exits non-root.

Linh: chown fixed the permission error. After that the browser flow wrote a token and `redwoodctl whoami --profile team-local` shows my user. Thanks. One more related thing: when I run `redwoodctl local serve --profile team-local` the local runtime claims "profile not found" unless I explicitly set `REDWOOD_PROFILE=team-local` in env. I expected the CLI flag to propagate to the local server.

Sam: Ah, CLI flags sometimes don't auto-inject into subprocess env for the local serve command. Workaround is `REDWOOD_PROFILE=team-local redwoodctl local serve` or explicitly set profile in config file under `defaults`.

SRE Bot: Note for docs: profile precedence is currently CLI flags > env vars > config file, but `local serve` spawns a separate process that reads ONLY env vars and config file (bug). Filing follow-up issue to unify precedence and ensure flags propagate.

Matt: Filed internal ticket DEVEX-891. We should: 1) add a warning in install notes about not running the installer with sudo, 2) add a quick recovery step (`chown`), 3) fix `local serve` to respect flags, and 4) add an onboarding checklist entry about REDWOOD_PROFILE vs CLI flags.

Linh: All good on my end now. Leaving a short note in the onboarding doc and the reproduce steps. Will ping infra to update the installer. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

Sam: Awesome. If anyone else hits it, drop the `redwoodctl --version` and `ls -la ~/.config/redwood` output here and we'll help.
